items.title: Tova Davidson, Executive Director, Sustainable Waterloo Region
notes:
Tova Davidson, Executive Director, Sustainable Waterloo Region (SWR), provided an update on the work that SWR is doing and their impact in the community. She elaborated on the CO2 reductions in the area related to the work that her organization does.

In reply to a question from the Committee, T. Davidson spoke to projects that result in savings for energy costs related to environmental engineering in buildings being conducted to preserve energy. She explained the collaborative efforts that SWR is engaged in with contributions from the development and construction community to enable the shift to environmentally friendly energy sources to happen.

Responding to questions from the Committee, T. Davidson provided clarification as to the merging of national and provincial net zero targets and the Region's progress in that regard. She also spoke to the relationship with School Boards and the education programs in place related to environmental work.

items.title: Pranavkumar Shukla, Kitchener
notes: The delegation spoke to transit issues related to his neighbourhood, specifically the lack of access to Grand River Transit (GRT) routes. He highlighted the various schools and businesses in the area which may benefit from greater access to transit.

items.title: Arnold Radford, Waterloo
notes:
The delegation spoke to protecting pedestrian neighbourhoods by enhancing safety. He spoke to concerns about bike lanes and other measures being implemented on roadways that affect safety, and expressed concerns related to the use of e-scooters and e-bikes.

Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services, provided further clarification as to the legislation which governs the usage of bicycles and similar type of vehicles on sidewalks.

Staff were asked to report on pedestrian safety measures and enforcement options within the Region.

items.title: Barry Green, Cambridge
notes: The delegation spoke to essentialness of the accessibility of the LRT, noting difficulties with transit and having to use multiple bus routes on a daily basis for travel.

items.title: Holden Sisak, Cambridge
notes: The delegation spoke to his positive experience with LRT and advocated for the expansion of the transit system into Cambridge.

items.title: Devin Sisak, EA, Barrier-free Cambridge
notes: The delegation spoke in support of the Phase II ION project, highlighting the critical nature of expanding into Cambridge.

items.title: Dan Clements, Member, Citizens for Cambridge
notes:
The delegation spoke on behalf of Citizens for Cambridge, and commended staff for the initial business case for phase II ION. He provided support for the plan for an increase in infrastructure, especially as it pertains to the ION LRT extension.

In reply to a question from the Committee, the delegation spoke to potential issues with turnout for public engagement in Cambridge.

items.title: David Terrance Fortin, Cambridge
notes:
The delegation spoke in favour of the ION Phase 2 extension into Cambridge, highlighting the benefits of mobility and support collaboration between campuses for post-secondary institutions. He elaborated on the design studies he has conducted with students and other community partners.

In reply to questions, the delegation emphasized the benefits of collaboration amongst several organizations, of which such collaboration his organization is deeply in favour of.

items.title: John Tennant, Kitchener
notes: The delegation spoke in favour of Councillor Rodrigues' motion listed on the agenda related to the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH). He provided multiple documents which spoke to rail-related infrastructure, which are attached to the minutes. He further added that staff should also consider a citizen committee to address overall rail-related strategies and associated infrastructure.

items.title: TSD-RTS-25-001, Stage 2 ION Initial Business Case Engagement Plan
notes:
Neil Malcolm, Director, Transit Services, introduced the report. Neil Malcolm, Director, Transit Services, provided a presentation elaborating on the ways in which staff will connect with residents on the Phase II ION project extension into Cambridge. He clarified the 'BRT versus LRT,' with BRT being a precursor to the ION light trail. The initial business case for the project is anticipated for November 2025.

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner clarified the timeline for the project. He indicated that Regional staff are already working with the provincial government on a submission to the federal government for funding.

The report was received for information.

TSD-TRP-25-012, Highland Road Noise Issues
notes:
D. Spooner provided an introduction to the report, and expanded on staff's recommendation based on the region's policy and the activity monitored at the relevant site. He elaborated on the potential costs associated with violating aspects of the noise policy and the adverse affects on the transportation budget. 

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner provided further clarification as to the various options available for residents, including construction of tight fences.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner spoke to road design guidelines and associated policies that assist in noise through acceleration.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - Councillor Matt Rodrigues
motions.text: WHEREAS the multi-year, multi-phase construction of the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH) and GO Expansion works may have impacts to community including, but not limited to, noise, traffic disruption, transit detours, or changes to existing rail operations; WHEREAS it is important for residents, local elected officials, local businesses, and community associations and service providers to have access to advance project information and updates and work collaboratively; THEREFORE be it resolved that the Commissioner of Transportation and Commissioner of Resident Experience, Strategy, and Communications report back to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee by the end of Q4 2025 to Outline plans on how the Region will update the community relative to KCTH, including how this information can include work to be undertaken by Metrolinx and other organizations; Provide opportunities for the Region to actively engage with residents, businesses, and BIA that are adjacent to KCTH, in order to address construction impacts and mitigation measures; Request that Metrolinx also actively participate in these engagement opportunities, for the construction works under its responsibility, while providing opportunities for the Region to amplify Metrolinx construction updates as they relate to KCTH and GO Expansion; and Establish consistent channels for the community to receive timely project information about all construction relative to the new GO Station and KCTH, across all organizations responsible for construction.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the multi-year, multi-phase construction of the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH) and GO Expansion works may have impacts to community including, but not limited to, noise, traffic disruption, transit detours, or changes to existing rail operations;
 
WHEREAS it is important for residents, local elected officials, local businesses, and community associations and service providers to have access to advance project information and updates and work collaboratively;
 
THEREFORE be it resolved that the Commissioner of Transportation and Commissioner of Resident Experience, Strategy, and Communications report back to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee by the end of Q4 2025 to

  1. Outline plans on how the Region will update the community relative to KCTH, including how this information can include work to be undertaken by Metrolinx and other organizations;
  2. Provide opportunities for the Region to actively engage with residents, businesses, and BIA that are adjacent to KCTH, in order to address construction impacts and mitigation measures;
  3. Request that Metrolinx also actively participate in these engagement opportunities, for the construction works under its responsibility, while providing opportunities for the Region to amplify Metrolinx construction updates as they relate to KCTH and GO Expansion; and
  4. Establish consistent channels for the community to receive timely project information about all construction relative to the new GO Station and KCTH, across all organizations responsible for construction.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - Councillor Colleen James
motions.text: WHEREAS ensuring the safety of all road users, including pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers, is a key priority for the Region of Waterloo; AND WHEREAS right turns on red lights can pose significant risks, particularly at major intersections with high volumes of traffic and documented collision histories; AND WHEREAS 89% of pedestrian collisions occur at signalized intersections, 56% of pedestrians struck by vehicles had the right of way, and 1 in 3 pedestrian collisions are caused by a turning vehicle; AND WHEREAS 74% of cycling collisions occur at intersections; AND WHEREAS intersections along regional arterial roads have experienced a number of vehicle and pedestrian-related incidents; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to report back on the feasibility, potential financial impacts, and implementation considerations of: Prohibiting right turns on red at key intersections along regional arterial roads with a documented history of high collision rates involving vehicles and/or pedestrians; and Introducing advanced pedestrian crossing signals (such as Leading Pedestrian Intervals) at those same intersections, which would allow pedestrians to begin crossing before vehicles receive a green light or turn signal; AND THAT the report include an analysis of collision data, potential safety benefits, impacts on traffic flow, operational and infrastructure considerations, consultation with area municipalities, and any best practices from comparable municipalities; AND THAT staff identify and include a preliminary list of possible candidate intersections for potential pilot implementation or further study of these safety measures.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS ensuring the safety of all road users, including pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers, is a key priority for the Region of Waterloo;

AND WHEREAS right turns on red lights can pose significant risks, particularly at major intersections with high volumes of traffic and documented collision histories;

AND WHEREAS 89% of pedestrian collisions occur at signalized intersections, 56% of pedestrians struck by vehicles had the right of way, and 1 in 3 pedestrian collisions are caused by a turning vehicle;

AND WHEREAS 74% of cycling collisions occur at intersections;

AND WHEREAS intersections along regional arterial roads have experienced a number of vehicle and pedestrian-related incidents;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to report back on the feasibility, potential financial impacts, and implementation considerations of:

Prohibiting right turns on red at key intersections along regional arterial roads with a documented history of high collision rates involving vehicles and/or pedestrians; and

Introducing advanced pedestrian crossing signals (such as Leading Pedestrian Intervals) at those same intersections, which would allow pedestrians to begin crossing before vehicles receive a green light or turn signal;

AND THAT the report include an analysis of collision data, potential safety benefits, impacts on traffic flow, operational and infrastructure considerations, consultation with area municipalities, and any best practices from comparable municipalities;

AND THAT staff identify and include a preliminary list of possible candidate intersections for potential pilot implementation or further study of these safety measures.
